notes: Step 1 parts were correct; no parts added or dropped.

Breadboard orientation: the image labels its upper half f-j and its lower half a-e, so the image's upper half is bank 'b' (rows f-j) and the lower half is bank 't' (rows a-e). The rails next to each half follow: upper rails are bp/bn and lower rails are tp/tn. In the image, the lower rail row nearer the board edge is the black line, so it is the negative rail. The red-line row is the positive rail.
Rail hole numbers are approximate, read from the image. Each rail is one strip, so the numbers do not change the electrical result.
Power: Uno 5V goes to the upper + rail (bp) and Uno GND goes to the upper - rail (bn). Two vertical jumpers on the right link the upper rails to the lower rails (bn to tn, bp to tp).

Button: pushbutton legs sit in columns 5 and 7 across the centre gap. Side 1 (column 5) is wired to + via wire3 (5V). Side 2 (column 7) goes to Uno pin 2 via the blue wire, and also to the 10K pull-down resistor r3. r3 runs from column 7 to column 10, and column 10 goes to the - rail via the black wire.
Sensor 1: the divider node is column 6 (bottom half). It holds FSR1 leg 1, r1 pin 1 and the A1 yellow wire. FSR1 leg 2 goes to the lower + rail. r1 pin 2 goes to the lower - rail.
Sensor 2: the divider node is column 16 (bottom half). It holds FSR2 leg 1, r2 pin 1 and the A0 yellow wire. FSR2 leg 2 goes to the lower + rail. r2 pin 2 goes to the lower - rail.

The image shows the A0 wire (outer loop) ending at column 16, the right-hand sensor, and the A1 wire (inner loop) ending at column 6, the left-hand sensor. I followed the image, although the schematic draws A0 with the left sensor.
Each resistor shares a strip with its FSR leg but sits in a different row, so no two leads share a hole. The exact rows are approximate.
The Uno GND wire is assigned to GND.2, the second GND pin in the power header.
